race.tagline: A high-altitude UCI qualifier built from three Pyrenean loops and a late trip to 2,006 metres.

climate.description: The course remains between roughly 1,760 and 2,006 metres, so race day can shift from sunny plateau conditions to cold wind or rain quickly. The race-specific forecast is not known in advance.
challenges: Wind on the open Cerdagne plateau
Fast temperature changes at mountain elevation
A long downhill finish after the highest point

terrain.primary: High-altitude gravel loops across the Cerdagne plateau
terrain.surface: The organizer describes a gravel course of wide-open mountain terrain, demanding climbs, and descending returns to Font-Romeu. Exact surface percentages are not published.

Three distinct loops through the Catalan Pyrenees

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The second-edition UCI qualifier scores on real altitude, 2,286 metres of climbing, and a strong competitive field. Its short history, rural access, and still-developing community keep it below elite status.

logistics.explanation: Font-Romeu is a mountain resort about 1 hour 40 minutes from Perpignan airport, with Carcassonne and Toulouse as alternatives. Resort lodging helps, but international riders still need a car or a carefully planned transfer into the Catalan Pyrenees.

length.explanation: The 100 km Granfondo fits the published 60-100 mile scoring band once converted to 62.1 miles. The compact distance means the 2,286 metres of climbing arrives with little flat recovery.

technicality.explanation: The official description promises mountain gravel, repeated descending returns, and a late descent from Pic de la Calma. It is mixed mountain terrain, but the organizer does not claim extreme singletrack or an enduro-style course.

elevation.explanation: The organizer publishes 2,286 metres, or about 7,500 feet, of climbing on the Granfondo. That sits squarely in the published 6,000-10,000-foot score-four band.

climate.explanation: A late-September race entirely above roughly 1,760 metres brings meaningful wind, cold-rain, and temperature-swing risk. The climate is a real preparation variable without being an inherently extreme-weather event.

altitude.explanation: Font-Romeu starts at roughly 1,760 metres and the course reaches 2,006 metres at Pic de la Calma. That keeps riders near or above 6,000 feet for much of the day, where sea-level athletes will notice the oxygen cost.

adventure.explanation: Three mountain loops link Mont-Louis, La Llagonne, Eyne 2600, and Pic de la Calma across the Cerdagne plateau. The high Pyrenean setting and late summit make the 100 km course feel larger than its distance.

prestige.explanation: UCI Gravel World Series status gives the second edition international relevance, and Romain Bardet won the inaugural 2025 event. Two editions do not yet create the history or cultural weight required for national-icon scoring.

race_quality.explanation: The organizer also runs the established 66 Degrés Sud road event, and the UCI publishes distinct qualifying courses by age category. That is professional structure, even though some race-day details remain unpublished.

experience.explanation: Repeated passages through Font-Romeu create visible race moments before a final trip to the 2,006-metre Pic de la Calma. The mountain scenery and descending finish should be memorable without inventing an atmosphere the second edition has not yet earned.

community.explanation: The event is capped at 600 and moved from Les Angles to Font-Romeu for its second edition. It has a serious regional base, but there is not yet evidence of a deep multi-year gravel culture around this specific race.

field_depth.explanation: UCI qualification places are awarded to the top 25 percent by category, and the inaugural winners included former WorldTour rider Romain Bardet. The qualifier structure attracts a stronger field than a normal regional event.

value.explanation: The race supplies a UCI qualification opportunity and a fully specified 100 km mountain course. The public page does not state a current entry price, so exceptional-value claims would be speculation.

expenses.explanation: International athletes face flights, a mountain transfer, and resort lodging in Font-Romeu. European riders can reduce that burden, but this is still a high-cost destination race for much of the catalog audience.

course_description.character: A three-loop, high-altitude UCI qualifier from Font-Romeu. The eastern loop reaches Col du Calvaire and returns at 39 km; the southern loop adds a 10 km climb and returns at 76 km; the final northern loop reaches Pic de la Calma at 2,006 m before a downhill finish.
course_description.signature_challenge: Arriving at the final 25 km with enough climbing power left for Pic de la Calma, then descending cleanly to Font-Romeu after a day spent near 6,000 feet.

suffering_zones.label: Col du Calvaire
suffering_zones.desc: The first loop reaches 1,856 metres near kilometre 36 before descending to the first finish-line passage.

suffering_zones.label: Southern-loop climb
suffering_zones.desc: A 10 km climb through the Eyne 2600 and Saint-Pierre-dels-Forcats sector builds the middle-race fatigue.

suffering_zones.label: Pic de la Calma
suffering_zones.desc: The hardest final loop reaches the 2,006-metre high point with roughly 12 km left before the downhill finish.

biased_opinion.summary: Do not read 100 km and expect a friendly half-day. The course packs 2,286 metres of climbing into three loops, never drops below meaningful altitude, and saves its highest point for the final 12 km. It is a young race, but the UCI field and Pyrenean course are already legitimate.
weaknesses: Current public page omits some operations details
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A strong Tier 2 choice for riders who want UCI stakes and altitude without an ultra-distance day. Train the climbing density, not just the mileage.

logistics.airport: Perpignan (PGF), approximately 1 hour 40 minutes by road; Carcassonne and Toulouse are alternatives
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Font-Romeu so race morning does not depend on a mountain transfer. The resort has hotels and apartments, but book before late-summer demand tightens.
logistics.transport: A car or prearranged transfer is the practical option from regional airports.
logistics.food: Font-Romeu has resort dining and grocery options; bring race nutrition that has already been tested at altitude.

history.origin_story: The event debuted in Les Angles in 2025 and moved to Font-Romeu for its second UCI Gravel World Series edition.
notable_moments: Romain Bardet and Axelle Dubau-Prévot won the inaugural 2025 edition.
history.reputation: A new high-altitude French UCI qualifier with immediate elite-field credibility.

guide_variables.race_terrain: High-altitude Pyrenean gravel across three climbing loops
guide_variables.race_weather: Early-autumn mountain conditions with wind and temperature swings
race_challenges: Late Pic de la Calma ascent

topics.climbing: Repeating long climbs with limited recovery
topics.descending: Descending after the final high point

marketplace_variables.race_hook: Six weeks to make the 2,286 metres survivable.
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: A Save My Race block for the high-altitude UCI qualifier in Font-Romeu.

non_negotiables.why: The 100 km course carries 2,286 metres of climbing across all three loops.
Most of race day stays near or above 1,760 metres.
The finish comes after descending from the course high point with 12 km remaining.

final_verdict.one_liner: A young UCI qualifier with grown-up altitude and 7,500 feet of climbing in only 62 miles.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if UCI age-group stakes and a compact mountain course appeal to you. Skip it if you cannot arrive with either altitude exposure or a conservative pacing plan.
final_verdict.alternatives: Wish One Millau for a lower-altitude French qualifier; The Majestics Gravel for a longer-established Alpine event.
